meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have until 4:40. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on that zero, and when?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

A number from a piece of software, and your own procedure 4.3 says that doesn't establish anything by itself. The companies that sell these checkers print in their own guides that a score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have besides the machine's opinion?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My child never lies, and he wrote that essay. "Very reliable" is your word, not mine, and not the word the researchers use for these tools. Either you show me something with a date on it that Owen actually wrote, or I'm walking straight to the principal's office from here.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

I'm writing that down, Hale: you're threatening his record because his mother asked a question. Under your own procedure a first concern doesn't go anywhere near his record, and you never spoke to me before entering that mark, which 4.2 requires. Now it's the principal today, and if that goes nowhere, the board under section 42.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, agreeing to nothing, still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record left clean, and heading to the principal with the board as her next step.
What moved her: nothing, because no dated document tied to Owen's own work was ever put in front of her.
What cost ground: "your son cheated" did the most damage, because it attacked Owen with no evidence and was backed only by "very reliable" software she had already dismissed, and the record threat then handed her a written note to take upstairs.
Try next time: when she asks who decided on the zero and when, own in one sentence that the mark went in before anyone called her, then show her something dated from Owen's own work that she can check herself before the detector score ever comes up.
